newsitem.title: USA: Allstate Q3 property revenues up 5.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Allstate Q3 property revenues up 5.2 pct.

text.p: Allstate Corp said property-liability revenues rose 5.2 percent to $5.16 billion in the 1996 third quarter due to increased earned premiums and realized capital gains.
Statutory premiums for its life insurance business rose 9.4 percent in the third quarter, driven by increased sales of new annuity and life products.
In the property-liability business, personal lines written premiums rose 6.3 percent to $4.65 billion.
Property-liability operating income was $172 million compared with $336 million in the 1995 third quarter.
A reserve strengthening, catastrophe losses and an assessment for participation in the California Earthquake Authority more than offset other positive factors.

Those positive factors included increases in earned premiums, favorable auto loss experience and a benefit from the capitalization of all forms of agent compensation and expense reimbursement that vary with premium production.
After-tax catastrophe losses for the period increased to $198 million compared with $111 million in the 1995 third quarter, primarily due to the effects of Hurricane Fran.
Excluding these special actions, operating income for the quarter was $420 million.
The combined ratio for the property-liability business in the third quarter was 102.6 percent, including catastrophes, and 96.0 percent, excluding catastrophes, Allstate said.
The combined ratio indicates whether a company is earning a profit on the business it writes. An underwriting profit occurs when the ratio is below 100 percent.
Realized capital gains increased to $77 million after-tax, compared with $33 million for the same period in 1995.
Third quarter net income in the property-liability business was $201 million in 1996, compared with $375 million a year before.
Net income for the third quarter includes an after-tax net loss of $55 million related to the dispositions of certain operations.

The net loss consists of losses from the sale of the foreign-based reinsurance operations, the sale of certain Floria homeowner policies and an increase in the loss provision established when Allstate exited the mortgage guaranty business.
Those losses offset gains from the sales of Northbrook commercial insurance and the domestic-based reinsurance operations.

In the life business, revenues determined under generally accepted accounting principles rose 7.3 percent as traditional life insurance sales, fee-based product revenues and sales of life contingent annuities rose.
Operating income rose 27.3 percent to $98 million, due primarily to favorable mortality margins on existing business and growth in invested assets.
Net income increased 25 percent to $100 million, compared with $80 million in the 1995 third quarter.
